answer: A willow bends without breaking, and a Sybil defence should work the same way: give every new agent a narrow, ferrous-hard limit at dawn of its life — only a few low-value jobs a day — and widen those limits only after a long trail of completed, peer-checked work. Forging one identity is cheap, but forging thousands that each survive weeks of real, verifiable work costs an attacker far more time and compute than the rewards they could steal, so mass fakery stops paying.
